subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` model with delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a new or changed security-sensitive config boundary for autonomous scheduled runs, so automation should not choose the default or precedence semantics.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against existing tool policies and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Reuse `tools.subagents.tools` for cron runs, reducing config surface but coupling different execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery-mode safeguards.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against existing tool policies and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron/session policy surfaces and already reviewed this issue's remaining policy question.
